beliefs.practice: Use a single shared MongoClient per Node.js process, enable the unified topology, and set maxPoolSize (e.g. ?maxPoolSize=50) in the connection string rather than creating clients per request.
Enforce TLS by using tls=true (or ssl=true) in the connection string and verify certificates (do not disable certificate validation).

Never commit DB credentials; store the DocumentDB connection string/username/password in Azure Key Vault and load at runtime (or use environment variables populated from Key Vault), and keep .env.example with placeholders only.
Create least-privilege database users: use a dedicated app user with only the minimum roles/privileges needed (read/write on the sample_retail_08 collections) rather than admin/root credentials.
Avoid string-building queries; use parameterized queries/driver APIs (filter objects) to prevent injection and ensure indexes are used (e.g., db.collection.find({ segmentId: segId })).
Create a scalar index on fields frequently filtered/sorted (e.g., segmentId, customerId, createdAt); for MongoDB API use createIndex({ segmentId: 1 }) before running lookups.

For vector search, define a dedicated embedding field (e.g., embeddings: [Float]) and create the provider-specified vector index (HNSW/IVF) with explicit parameters (e.g., index type HNSW, M=16, efConstruction=200) appropriate for your recall/latency needs.
Normalize and fix embedding dimensionality on write (reject or pad vectors with wrong dimension) and optionally store L2-normalized vectors if you plan to use dot-product for cosine similarity.

Use partial or sparse indexes for optional large fields (like embeddings) so only documents that contain embeddings are indexed, preventing index bloat: createIndex({ embeddings: 1 }, { sparse: true }) or provider equivalent.
Implement retry logic that handles transient network errors and 429 (rate limiting) responses with exponential backoff, honoring the Retry-After header when present.

Monitor request units / consumed throughput and configure autoscale or increase provisioned throughput for the sample_retail_08 database/collections to accommodate vector search and LLM-generation bursts; add alerts on RU consumption.
Keep documents well under the MongoDB 16MB document limit; store large attachments (images, logs) in Azure Blob Storage and reference them from documents rather than embedding large binary blobs.
When doing pagination avoid large skip offsets; use range-based pagination or a stable sort key (e.g., createdAt + _id bookmark) to page through results efficiently.
Create indexes required by any query patterns before seeding/using the dataset (run createIndex in seed/provision script) and verify index existence with listIndexes as part of deployment validation.
Use TTL indexes for ephemeral campaign drafts or staging documents (e.g., createIndex({ expireAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 0 })) to automatically expire old campaign drafts.

Set an appropriate writeConcern (and readPreference) for the workload: majority writeConcern if you need cross-replica durability; otherwise accept acknowledged writes for reduced latency—explicitly set in driver options.
Use idempotent writes or an upsert pattern (e.g., updateOne(filter, { $set: doc }, { upsert: true })) for campaign document writes so retries do not create duplicates.
Restrict network access to the cluster using firewall rules, VNet integration, or private endpoints; do not expose the DocumentDB/MongoDB endpoint publicly to the internet for production workloads.
Instrument and log slow queries and index usage (use explain() / query plan tools) and address any queries that do collection scans by adding appropriate indexes.

Do not include raw PII in prompts or logs; redact or hash personally-identifiable fields before sending to LLMs and when storing generated drafts include only the minimal required customer attributes (or encrypt sensitive fields at rest).
Pre-create any vector indexes and wait for the index build to complete before running similarity queries; include an index-building and verification step in your seed/provisioning script.
Use partial projection in reads to fetch only the fields needed for prompt engineering (e.g., projection { purchaseHistory: 1, preferences: 1 }) to reduce bandwidth and RU/IO cost.

Enable and test application-level retries for transient failures but avoid retrying non-idempotent multi-document transactions unless you can guarantee idempotency or use an application-level dedup token.

Include a provisioning script that creates collections with the intended throughput/indexes and a verification script that calls listCollections/listIndexes and a short sample query to confirm connectivity and permissions.
Don’t log or persist the raw DocumentDB connection string or SAS tokens; if you must persist connection metadata use Key Vault references or managed identity, and rotate credentials regularly.
